title: Effective Node-Level Anomaly Detection in HPC Systems via Coarse-Grained Clustering and Fine-Grained Model Sharing
problem: Large-scale HPC systems experience performance degradation and failures; anomaly detection at node-level is challenged by massive scales, frequent job transitions, and complex patterns.
motivation: Unexpected failures impact scientific research; unsupervised anomaly detection avoids manual labeling overhead and adapts to evolving system behavior.
method: NodeSentry: unsupervised framework combining coarse-grained clustering and fine-grained model sharing for scalable node-level anomaly detection.
key_novelty: Novel model sharing strategy reduces training overhead 45.69% while achieving F1-score >0.876; 0.560 average improvement over baselines.
contributions: Coarse-grained clustering and fine-grained model sharing architecture
45.69% reduction in training overhead vs. baselines
Open-source codebase and HPC-specific clustering adjustment tool
workloads: Node-level performance monitoring and anomaly detection
limitations: Unsupervised; limited to node-level (not application-level); requires sufficient data; model sharing effectiveness depends on cluster homogeneity.
